artists.biography:
Menswear (sometimes written "Menswe@r") were a Britpop band formed in October 1994 from Camden in London.

The beginnings of the band were a feature in a Select article about a supposed London mod revival led by Graham Coxon. Two individuals closely associated with the burgeoning Britpop scene, Chris Gentry and Johnny Dean, made references to a "top new unsigned band" (Menswear), an act which did not yet exist.

They later appeared on the cover of Melody Maker before they had released any material. Their dress sense was Mod (tight fitting suits etc.) whilst their music was influenced by both Blur's second album Modern Life Is Rubbish and Elastica. Gentry and Dean had a single song - called "Daydreamer" - but soon recruited friend Simon White, who contributed "I'll Manage Somehow" to add to the setlist necessary for their upcoming debut gig at a Britpop-oriented club on Regent Street called Smashing.

perplexity.description:
Nuisance is the debut studio album by British rock band Menswear, released on 24 October 1995 by the Laurel label, a subsidiary of London Records. The album is rooted in the Britpop and indie rock styles characteristic of mid-1990s British music, featuring catchy guitar-driven melodies and youthful, energetic vocals. Menswear's sound on Nuisance reflects the vibrant Camden music scene of the time, blending jangly guitars with a pop sensibility that aligned them with contemporaries in the Britpop movement.

As Menswear's first full-length release, Nuisance marked the band's commercial breakthrough, reaching number 11 on the UK Albums Chart. It spawned five singles, including their highest-charting hit "Being Brave," which reached the UK top 10 in 1996. Despite mixed critical reception—some critics viewed the band as more style than substance—the album captured the spirit of mid-90s Britpop and gained a dedicated fanbase. Over time, Nuisance has been revisited as a notable artifact of the era, with anniversary reissues highlighting its enduring appeal within the genre.
